findings.review: The communion/intercession claims are anchored most directly in Q122–123. Several other browse-index numbers concern historical membership distinctions rather than the central communion argument.
The 1912 Eucharistic fasting rule is historical discipline and must not be displayed as current universally applicable practice.
Marriage procedures, including civil-form discussion, require present-day applicable canon and civil law before practical instruction.
The moral conscience claims are grounded directly in Veritatis splendor 60–61. The compact index's sin taxonomy is background, not a direct conscience definition.

The complete Q385 answer explicitly mentions sacramentals, holy water and blessings. Its question stem alone is misleading. The later Catechism gives the fuller distinction between sacramentals and sacraments.
Liturgical-year theology needs Mediator Dei 165; Sunday and fasting precepts in the 1912 Catechism are not the entire theology. Specific fasting discipline may have changed.
